rows: Proprietor (elf of uncertain but clearly not-young age, long institutional history of elven ownership, soft-voiced, emotionally aware of the common room, known to regulars by name, called 'the keeper' by strangers). Bartender (traditionally the proprietor himself, with junior assistance from sun-elf woman in her second century at peak evenings, institutional memory for patrons — returning after a decade, patron's preferred wine is remembered). Kitchen: half-elven cook + 2 elven assistants. Rotating musician roster (resident harpist 4 nights/week; other instruments occasional; traveling performers when they come through). No standing martial garrison — the tavern's protection is institutional respectability, permanent sound-wards on private rooms, enchanted continual-light lamps (renewed by resident druid at quarterly maintenance), and the elven community's collective standing as a Waterdhavian population segment. 6 upper-floor guest rooms for traveling elves. Walled back garden ~40x30 ft (rowan, silver birches, herb plantings, stone bench) open to patrons in summer.

Principal elven social establishment in Waterdeep. North Ward, 2-story stone-and-timber building, slate roof. Name from single polished moonstone set into silver lintel above front door (catches light unusually, blessed at establishment by High Priestess of the House of the Moon per local legend). Carved oak door with silver-inlay leaf-and-vine tracery. Interior: common room 50x25 ft, western-wall bar, aged oak paneling, tapestries of woodland scenes and abstracted leaf patterns, enchanted continual-light lamps, north-wall stone fireplace with carved mantle. Wine selection: Evermeet when available (increasingly rare), Cormanthor, Silver Marches, Silverymoon-area elvish vineyards. Elvish cuisine adapted for mixed clientele (breads, aged cheeses, cured meats, seasonal greens, honey-nut pastries). Quiet music most evenings (resident harpist 4 nights/week + rotating performers). Two sound-warded private dining rooms at rear for business/diplomatic/social privacy — rentable at premium. 6 upper-floor guest rooms for traveling elves. Back walled garden with rowan, silver birches, herb plantings. Tavern runs on implicit code of elven courtesy — does not refuse non-elven patrons but filters by self-selection; loud patrons find their drinks slow in arriving. Campaign relevance: Shi'van cannot visit directly (institutional elven-drow tensions too deep); Seren Nightbloom's moon-elf seamstress cover is ideal for ambient listening; Marcel Dior'Elle welcomed without being regular (sun-elf, Institut-aligned, can rent private rooms for commercial engagements); Pharyn Baen'und latent invitation potential through elven noble family channel; Cerulean Circle membership-overlap makes Elfstone second-best signal-propagation venue after direct Circle access; private rooms are rare North Ward sound-warded discreet-dining asset.
WotC canon: Waterdeep and the North (2E), Volo's Guide to Waterdeep (2E), City of Splendors: Waterdeep (3.5E boxed set), various FR elven-community references.

Clan Stoneshaft (dwarven). Borgan Stonebreaker (seneschal), Vendra Goldmark (quartermaster), Hallund Ironpen (clerk). Independent clan counter-intelligence. Underdark-adjacent dwarven ground — Hunzrin does not have reliable observation here.

Dwarven clan hold on the Dessarin corridor. 'Thornhold' is the legacy reference name; STONESHAFT HOLD is canonical. Waystation support contract signed Session 35, 22nd Marpenoth 1493 DR (Day 728), at 120 gp/yr tripwire rate — southbound caravan anchor for the Yartar-avoiding corridor. Key personnel: Borgan Stonebreaker (seneschal), Vendra Goldmark (quartermaster), Hallund Ironpen (clerk). Shi'van deposited Margaster/Hunzrin intelligence; logged as clan-credit honoured at discretion. Received in exchange: mould-fault rubbing of forged Yartar Merchants' Guild seal used on Shaw/Hargrove credentials — identifies the single Margaster-sourced Waterdhavian forgery shop. Underdark-adjacent dwarven ground with independent counter-intelligence; Hunzrin has no reliable observation here. Jarlaxle/BD will register the contract via incidental trade observation ~Day 740. Merileth filing decision pending (public vs private) on the forgery rubbings; will determine Margaster arrival timing on the shop ID.

Early 1495 DR: ~800 Bloodaxe-affiliated security personnel on rotating deployment, Captain Gerald Westmont's immediate staff ~40, workshop / quartermaster / logistics / medical / crystal-network crews ~120 combined. ~2,000 construction workers (60% human, 30% dwarf, 10% other) in mixed barracks and tent encampments (non-military). Devil construction crews operate nights per Zariel contract. Expected full operational garrison: 5,000 troops + support.

Active multi-level ziggurat fortress under construction in the northeastern Neverwinter Woods pass. Design closes the pass entirely: 800 ft wide × 400 ft north-south × 200 ft deep excavation forming artificial mountain ziggurat with 4-level progression (Foundation Plateau / Rampart Terrace / Sustenance Circle / Command Apex) plus underground complex for 1,000+ personnel. Aluminum-cast artillery stockpiled for 5-mile-radius dominance. At Early 1495 DR ~Month 12-14 of 24-month supernatural-speed construction (Zariel devil-contract labor). Level 1 near complete; Level 2 active; Levels 3-4 planned. Secret contents: aluminum stockpile, preserved pre-elven Garden Keeper carvings, and (unknown to all parties) House Baen'und chronicle buried in southeast foundation corner. Four cosmological powers have converging interests: Arik (northern consolidation), Zariel (devil-labor proof-of-concept), Garden Keeper (ancient carvings attention), Odin (observed via Sister Catherine + raven network). Key personnel: Foreman Magnus Ironfoot (dwarf, careful ignorance), Captain Gerald Westmont (security, briefed on devils), Sister Catherine of Odin (shrine keeper, divine observer), Mysterious Supervisors (Arik's devil overseers). Active threats: weekly orc scouting probes, drow infiltration, supply sabotage, political opposition in Neverwinter, ancient disturbances from deep vault carvings.

No standing presence. Kenafin embedded asset (provisionally Thessaly Wren) serviced the drop until Day 620 dormancy. BD actively collecting (Kimmuriel Oblodra reading product). Firth not authorized for active surveillance at current campaign time. Second Kenafin operative in Waterdeep signaled distress at adjacent chalk mark (Blackstaff Alley/Nethpranter Row corner) — Seren's response deferred.

Kenafin embedded theological assessor's dead drop. Alley behind Coffinmaker's shop, Nethpranter Street, Waterdeep. Identified by Shi'van Session 21 via Thaelen Korr pipeline. Embedded asset provisionally identified as Thessaly Wren (Session 22 Chat 8, d20=18). Current status: DORMANT since Day 620 (final report at Plinth, not here). BD collecting from this drop — Session 33 reframe establishes BD as intermediate intelligence layer. Adjacent site: chalk mark at Blackstaff Alley/Nethpranter Row corner (distress signal from second Kenafin operative in Waterdeep, Session 28 Seren discovery).

Castle Waterdeep Griffon Cavalry (standing detachment at Mount Waterdeep Barracks at ~200 ft elevation on eastern face, working birds roosting at the Castle aerie, patrol upper slopes, serve as forward air-defense position). Four Walking Statues (massive stone constructs ~90 ft tall carved into mountain flanks at strategic elevations, dormant under normal conditions, activation by Open Lord authority or Archmage emergency writ only, last documented activation centuries past). Hermits, scholars from the Font of Knowledge, occasional climbers at middle and upper elevations (unregistered, tolerated, patrolled). No permanent settlement above residential-construction line. No standing martial garrison on upper mountain — the mountain's defense is its mass, its cliffs, its statues, and the Cavalry's aerial cover.

The mountain that is Waterdeep's foundation. Single stone massif rising ~1000 ft from the coast at the city's western edge. Western face: sheer sea cliff (200-300 ft vertical to Sea of Swords, uncolonized, defensive). Eastern face: gradual slope into Castle Ward, residential construction up to a certain elevation then wild ground. Northern ridge meets Trollwalls; southern flank shelters harbor. Summit holds small stone shrine of uncertain dedication (predates surviving records, rebuilt many times). Castle Waterdeep at the mountain's eastern foot; Undermountain megadungeon beneath the mountain's mass (accessed via the Yawning Portal's Well — the canonical city-facing entry). Four Walking Statues carved into mountain flanks at strategic elevations (each ~90 ft tall humanoid stone construct animate in historical defense crises, dormant under normal conditions, activation restricted to Open Lord/Archmage authority). Mount Waterdeep Barracks at ~200 ft elevation houses Griffon Cavalry detachment. Mountain stone has been Waterdeep's building material for a thousand years — quarries on southern/eastern flanks provide ongoing supply. Baen Construction Waterdeep work uses Mount Waterdeep stone as standard. Campaign relevance: geographic grounding for all westward scenes, Undermountain access vector (latent), stone quarry baseline for construction economics, Griffon Cavalry latent institutional relationship through Castle Waterdeep command floor, symbolic backdrop for the city's foundational permanence.
WotC canon: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist (5E), Dungeon of the Mad Mage (5E), City of Splendors: Waterdeep (3.5E), Volo's Guide to Waterdeep (2E), Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3E.

No standing garrison within the library itself. Asmodeus is sole resident principal. Ancillary staff: pit fiend administrative operators (resident in Nessus broadly; rarely present in the library during audiences). Corridor security detail: standing operatives executing evaluation protocols ('permitted attack' testing infrastructure) on visiting delegations — canonical, count unspecified, operating under standing orders. No mortal permanent residents; no mortal garrisoned forces; no ordinary population. All presence in the library is by Asmodeus's explicit summons or grant.

Audience chamber of Asmodeus, Lord of the Ninth. Sixty-foot circular library within Nessus (likely Malsheem proper; canonically unspecified). Floor-to-ceiling bookshelves spanning every civilization the Nine Hells have contacted across millennia; dark stone domed ceiling (unmarked, only textless surface); polished obsidian floor; uniform warm illumination from no visible source. Central desk in nearly-black wood with one open book, inkwell, and pen. No throne. Asmodeus appears as a man in his late fifties, brown eyes 'the color of good leather,' simple dark red robes, no regalia. Canonical first audience (Asmodeus Audience Framework): Arik + 21-member delegation; chairs pre-placed and sized to each delegate's measurements (grade from corridor evaluation testing); five-beat negotiation structure resulted in Warborn contract extension, Demiurge transfer framework (contingent), Dalelands war commitment from Arik, no-predation mutual exclusion clause (comprehensive ban on all cosmological predation within Baen sovereign territory, expands automatically with conquest, applies to all parties including Hell), and one uncashed question (any topic, answered truthfully by Asmodeus at Arik's timing — remains held). Asmodeus accepted the exclusion on long-horizon calculation that proof of mortal civilization operating outside divine-infernal framework is worth more than soul revenue exclusion costs. Corridor approach is evaluation zone (canonical 'permitted attack' testing). Scry-warding absolute. Minor location per page-schema (per-visit Model B ambient tables).

Master Goldweaver (Senior Appraiser, principal authority on high-value specimens, signature on ESAMT ruby certification at 1,010,000gp). Senior Masters' Council (12-member adjudicative body, meets monthly in second-floor chamber). Guild porter at the threshold during business hours. Three registry clerks at ground-floor desks. Night watchmen from guild's own staff. Registered member body including Shi'van Baen'und (Master Associate standing via Silverhair workshop profit-share). Archive and vault staff for third-floor secure storage. No standing martial garrison — security is institutional and procedural, backed by guild discipline, standard commercial-grade locks, and scrying-resistance on appraisal chambers.

Jewelers' Guild Hall of Waterdeep. Diamond Street, Castle Ward. Three-story limestone building. Ground floor: public registry hall (clerks' desks, consultation benches, filing cabinets, members file new commissions and collect certifications here), locked registry vault holding master records back to the guild's charter. First floor: four private appraisal chambers along central corridor, soundproofed and scrying-warded, Master Goldweaver works from the corridor's northern chamber. Second floor: Senior Masters' Council meeting chamber, attached archive (charter documents, disciplinary records, master pattern book). Third floor: secure storage and working archive (pieces held in trust, appraisal-dispute holdings, reference specimens, active commission registry separate from public records). Master Goldweaver certified the flawless million-gold ruby anchoring the Enhanced Strategic Asset Management Trust (1,010,000gp) — the foundational appraisal on which Shi'van's 3,000,000gp borrowing capacity rests. Shi'van registered as Master Associate (via Silverhair workshop profit-share); all her commercial pieces (Evening's Edge, Verðandi Collar, Eye of Verðandi Phase 5, Eye of Dagaz in progress, protection-line commissions routing through the Atelier) are on the registry here. Session 8B decision 'all stones through guild registry — customer AND family editions, no exceptions' is operative institutional doctrine. Toril Shield Assurance's Guardian Pledge hypothecation uses the appraisal pipeline that runs through this Hall. Farid al-Rashid at Starfall Gems (Trades Ward nephew of the al-Rashid Calimshan mineral network) is an unresolved Institut-sponsorship thread that would route through House of Gems licensing.
ESAMT Trust document (Merileth Dawntracker); Session 8B all-stones-through-registry decision; Session 22 Chat 5 al-Rashid/Farid surfacing; Silverhair Artistic Metals Commission Ledger.

Tower Commander (senior Waterdeep Guard Naval Detachment officer on extended Seatower rotation, reports to Castle Waterdeep naval command, authority over approach clearance and rapid-response deployment). Standing garrison ~50 personnel (3-month rotations). ~8 Signal Officers (flag-signal protocols, semaphore, lantern codes, messenger-bird dispatch, emergency communication — institutional memory of harbor-communication codes). ~6 Weapons Officers (ballista operation and maintenance, specialist training). ~8 Dockmaster and launch crew (supply dock, fast launch for pilot-skiff coordination and messenger deployment). Weapons: 3 ballistas standing deployment, 2 reserve (~400 yard effective range), arrow-slit batteries permanently manned during watch, alert bells always ready. Three-month supply reserves (food, fresh water cistern, munitions, rope/rigging). Observation watch continuous — never pauses.

Harbor defense fortress at mouth of Deepwater Harbor. Stone tower on rocky islet ~200 yards off eastern harbor mouth. Islet ~100x60 yards, tower occupies most of habitable surface, small leeward supply dock. Tower 80 ft above islet peak (40 ft above high tide), granite construction matching Mount Waterdeep quarry, walls 15-20 ft thick at base, narrower at upper stories, slope-walled base for grappling resistance, first accessible level at ~25 ft. Five levels + rooftop: ground (supply cellar, water cistern, munitions, tunnel to dock), 1st-2nd (garrison quarters, officers, mess, armory, infirmary), 3rd (signal chamber — operational heart, command), 4th (weapons platform — ballistas, arrow batteries, alert bells), 5th + rooftop (observation, spyglasses, lantern array). Named for Lord Balaeros, historical Waterdhavian naval defender (details archived at Font of Knowledge). Strategic role: first-contact authority for all harbor approach, continuous observation, signal coordination with Harbor Master's Office, rapid-response coordination with Bloodaxe Rapid Response + Lords' Alliance naval. Harbor attack response (Delegation-era): Tower provided early observation and signal alert, Bloodaxe deployed in 15 minutes, 3 vessels captured. Emergency alert bell has not rung in earnest in living memory. Campaign relevance: pure strategic infrastructure, no Shi'van direct interface at Day 729. Observation records are latent intelligence asset (vessel-arrival logs accessible by institutional writ). Harper delegation arrival pathway. Lord Balaeros historical research touches Sage Kellam's broader Waterdhavian institutional history work at Font of Knowledge.
WotC canon: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist (5E), City of Splendors: Waterdeep (3.5E), Volo's Guide to Waterdeep (2E), Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3E.

No surface authority. Jurisdictionally external to Waterdeep. The Skulls of Skullport (3 floating quasi-sentient skulls, historically neutrality enforcers, apprentices of Halaster Blackcloak who survived catastrophic transformation, currently reduced in activity but still present, capable of speech and destructive magic if provoked). Xanathar Guild growing institutional presence (expanding dominance, primary surface-criminal overlay, Guild's beholder leader resident in upper Undermountain). Zhentarim older commercial presence (trade networks, mercantile reach). Harpers undercover observation (monitor slave trade, Zhentarim ops, Xanathar expansion). Bregan D'aerthe commercial operator (Jarlaxle's standing interest, Arik-side aluminum trade logistics). Non-BD drow houses, duergar traders, beholders, mind flayer agents, miscellaneous Underdark powers. The Boneboard (informal merchant council, commercial dispute resolution, advisory not binding, respected because alternative is violence). Population 2000-4000 permanent + rotating transient (traders/smugglers/slavers/adventurers). Multi-racial: drow, duergar, beholders, mind flayers, humanoids of all surface origins, formorians, dragons' emissaries.

Subterranean port city on Undermountain Level 3. Vast cavern system (~5 miles interior), ceiling 60-300 ft, flat central floor rising to gallery levels. River Sargauth enters through Firegulp waterfall (northeastern wellhead), exits via lower passages to distant waters. Districts: Porthaven (waterfront docks, cargo handling, day-and-night shifts), Marketwall (central commercial gallery district, shops/taverns/flesh-markets/magical-goods), Slave Market (flesh-trade section, operates openly, significant portion of city's economy), Fluted Tower (mixed residential/administrative, eastern wall), Skulls' Chamber (gallery-level sacred space), Lower Passages (routes to Undermountain 4-5), Upper Ways (Yawning Portal public route, Chamber of Mournful Dead restricted route, lesser-known stair-and-tunnel routes). Jurisdictionally external to Waterdeep — no Masked Lords/Open Lord/Watchful Order/Watch jurisdiction. Skulls of Skullport (3 Halaster-apprentice remnants) historically enforced neutrality, currently reduced. Xanathar Guild growing dominance. Zhentarim older commercial presence. Harpers undercover. Bregan D'aerthe commercial. Commerce-over-violence tradition stabilizer. For Shi'van operations: not entered. Drow cover does not transplant (surface-integrated drow reads as suspicious in Skullport). BD channel endpoint (Valas operational line reaches Skullport via BD). Arik operational overlap (aluminum trade logistics almost certainly touch Skullport, unsurfaced sibling asymmetry). Petra Voss / Ship Kurth Fish St thread potentially terminates in Skullport commercial identities. Mistshore-Skullport contractor pipeline (Xanathar Guild recruiters deliver bodies from Mistshore, Firth Observer Network traces). Merileth's Northwatch Consulting occasional Skullport-sourced intel via intermediaries. Harper-alliance proxy via Laeral is feasible institutional pathway for future action but not currently operational.
WotC canon: Skullport (2E boxed set), City of Splendors: Waterdeep (3.5E), Waterdeep: Dragon Heist (5E), Dungeon of the Mad Mage (5E), Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3E.

No standing empire garrison in the forest proper. Way-station Bloodaxe details: ~12 stations × 6-12 operatives each = ~100-140 security personnel distributed along the Timber Road. Emergency reinforcement: a Bloodaxe mobile company can deploy from Neverwinter within two days; from Silverymoon within three. Veil operatives on ongoing surveillance deployment (engineered-lycanthropy investigation, secondary shadow-feeder monitoring) — count unspecified, field-rotation basis. Moonwood Glade has no garrison; its pre-human wardings are the security.

Ancient forest between Neverwinter-area and Silver Marches approaches. Contains Moonwood Glade — pre-human warded neutral meeting ground with absolute anti-scrying, consent-required teleportation, and conversation privacy enchantments. Silver-barked trees in natural amphitheater pattern 'too regular for coincidence'; draconic-accommodating stone landing pads; phosphorescent underbrush. Canonical Glade use: 28 Flamerule 1494 DR — Arik Baen's summit with the gold dragon Aurixilath, staged under Ulthaxor transport with Frieren + Lirien as attendants. Summit established preliminary metallic-dragon alliance against the Garden Keeper and Valdraxxis. Current Baen infrastructure: Timber Road (3-wagons-abreast, 120 miles Neverwinter to Silverymoon, 12 way-stations with Bloodaxe security, crystal communication nodes, refugee corridor during recent Silver Marches crisis). Active threat: engineered lycanthropy operation — unidentified party creating forced werewolves, evidence surfaced via blood forensics (Sania Valmorra hematomantic analysis), perpetrator not yet identified, Veil monitoring ongoing. Forest's druidic presence has not yet been canonically engaged. Glade remains available for future ancient-power diplomacy (Keeper contact, Valdraxxis operations, continental elvish/fey envoys).
conversation canon (Aurixilath summit + Silver Marches exodus scenes); no dedicated project-knowledge .md file

No permanent staff. Senior seamstresses rotate from Institut floor as protection commissions require (Rosalie Hatch schedules). Shi'van, Rosalie, and Firth carry keys. Marcel has key, rarely visits. Ward-thresholds at both entrances (Pharyn installation).

Original Baen'und workshop, predating the Institut. Three-story commercial building on Moonstar Lane, North Ward, ~8,000 sq ft + basement. Ground floor: traditional custom workshop (4-5 senior seamstresses rotating from Institut), public consultation, Shi'van's personal workbench. Second floor: three discrete fitting chambers, separate alley entrance, protection network hub — 17 noblewomen fitted, zero successful attacks since implementation. Trauma-sensitive fitting protocols developed here. Third floor: locked at all times (Shi'van + Rosalie keys only). Protection garments inventory (code names, never real names), confidential client files, high-value materials (star-iron wire, phase spider silk, mithril thread). Basement: panic room / safe house for up to 4 people — 14-hour emergency shelter, medical supplies, 500gp emergency funds, identity papers, sending stone to estate. Hidden exit to chandler's cellar two buildings east (chandler paid 25gp/quarter retainer through Northwatch Advisory, doesn't know what's in his wall). Used once for a protection client's domestic emergency.

The Atelier is trust. The Institut is production. The showroom is presentation. Protection network operates here because the building provides discrete access, invisible client flow, and security no other facility matches.

Callum Firth (primary authority). Brannock (field operative, prisoner delivery). Tesserly (field operative, senior access). Access compartmentalized to Firth tight circle. One trained-operative hold capacity confirmed (Margaster specialist, Day 584–592+). Covered by 550gp/month Observer Network budget.

Observer Network holding location and sensitive-meeting safehouse. Cellar at 14 Nethpranter Street, Waterdeep. Established Session 21 Day 584 when Firth's coverage expanded to 550gp/month. Held the Margaster specialist through Commerce Court hearing period. Hosted Peri emissary Doyle coordination meeting (Session 27 Day 630). Same street as the Kenafin dead drop alley (behind Coffinmaker's shop) — proximity creates mild counter-surveillance exposure but Firth tradecraft compensates. Secondary function: sensitive Observer Network meetings off Estate/tavern record. Compartmentalized to Firth, Brannock, Tesserly, Doyle (Peri), Shi'van. Not shared with Marcel, Einar, Merileth, Edmund, Violet, Silverhair, staff, Seren.

Vajra Safahr (Archmage of Waterdeep, bearer of the Blackstaff, principal resident). Senior membership of the Watchful Order of Magists and Protectors operating from the Tower's adjudication, research, and licensing functions. Tower wards (extra-dimensional architecture — larger on the inside, reconfiguring stair arrangements, institutional-grade magical defenses that scale with threat). Fixed teleportation circles on a dedicated floor, institutionally controlled. Watchful Order membership at large (non-resident, but operationally tied to the Tower). No standing martial garrison — the Tower's defenses are magical, and the institutional authority of the Blackstaff office is the deeper deterrent.

Seat of the Archmage of Waterdeep. Castle Ward. Dark stone tower with extra-dimensional interior (larger on the inside, reconfiguring passageways). Headquarters of the Watchful Order of Magists and Protectors — Waterdeep's institutional wizards' guild. Current Blackstaff: Vajra Safahr. Signature property of the building: it is institutionally impossible to force entry. Teleportation circles on dedicated floor are part of the Sword Coast's fixed-installation long-range travel backbone — institutional control of teleportation is part of the Tower's operational authority. Institut de Tissage Arcanique holds a 2,000,000gp research partnership with the Watchful Order (memory thread applications, joint facility development, academic credibility). Archmage Torrino is Shi'van's weekly magical instructor; he is a Watchful Order member operating from his own tower rather than Blackstaff Tower proper, but his institutional affiliation routes through this building. Fenwick Tanglestone conducted translocation research here as Senior Conjurer before his departure — his final experiment destabilized Tower teleportation infrastructure for 11 minutes (Blackstaff Tower Incident). Tower's standing offer: return under institutional control, which Fenwick has refused. Silverhair's 40-piece Laeral ward-anchor commission (Session 9 Day 545) was coordinated with the Tower's municipal ward program. Vajra has no direct personal relationship with Shi'van at Day 729; the Waterdeep parent page flags 'offered potential future magical cooperation, monitoring magical developments in Northern Crown territory.' The relationship is latent and institutional rather than personal.
Waterdeep parent page (2fbe8214-84b0-81a8); Institut page (347e8214-84b0-81a8); Fenwick Tanglestone character sheet; Session 29 Section 14 ordinance analysis.

Ancient elven forest kingdom east of the Dalelands. Capital Myth Drannor (fallen 714 DR, contested rebuilding). At Early 1495 DR: contested and actively dying from the Verdant Corruption — Feywild seal broke ~1492 DR, carnivorous vegetation spreading at 1 mile/month, ~40 square miles consumed, 10-year countdown to total heartland loss. Four-zone gradient from fringe (Dales border) through interior to Myth Drannor / heart (Zone 4, reality destabilization, Cult of the Dragon dracolich candidate lair, likely Shepherd substrate anchor location). Sitting Coronal government failing. Three sitting Royal Council members secretly defected to Elara Baen'del (constitutional crisis timed weapon) + Marshal-Commander Thessian Autumnleaf (400yr military command) + Royal Archives = Elara's legitimacy infrastructure operating from Longsaddle Valley. Yggdrasil methodology (proven at Forgedeep, scaled at Longsaddle) is the only known counter to the Corruption. Leverage play: 'Support Elara, get salvation' — Cormanthor's sitting government chooses between backing her claim (reclamation) or inaction (forest dies). Reclamation campaign is forward-horizon (likely post-1497-1498 continental war): Longsaddle proof-of-concept → Dalelands corridor buildout → Jörmun expedition force into Zones 3-4 → Yggdrasil deployment at scale → Elara succession activation. Drow Underdark access canonically penetrates forest roots; druidic circles compromised or in retreat; Sembian commercial pressure from south; Zhentarim cells on Zone 1-2 fringe; Cult of the Dragon Zone 3-4. Dynasty arc: Elara + Arik mixed drow/moon elf heirs unprecedented, 400+ year joint rule possible per canonical Dynasty Compendium through 1620 DR.

Durnan (owner, proprietor, long-lived former Undermountain adventurer, famously laconic, known to every Open Lord across his Portal tenure). The Missus (Durnan's wife, runs the kitchen, accepts tabs). Winch operator on duty (unnamed rotating staff, maintains the Well ascent/descent assembly). Mirt the Moneylender (frequent patron at central common-room table when in Waterdeep, former Harper, extensive Waterdhavian connections). Bonnie (common-floor bartender rotating staff). Regular clientele: adventurers bound for or returning from Undermountain, merchants brokering equipment and information, Font of Knowledge scholars researching dungeon lore, Harpers using the Portal as rendezvous cover. No standing martial garrison — Durnan's quarterstaff behind the bar is the deterrent, plus the collective understanding that the Portal's peace is worth keeping.

Most famous tavern in Waterdeep. Castle Ward, corner lot, short walk from the Market and Castle Waterdeep. Named for the 40-foot well in the rear courtyard that opens onto the first level of Undermountain — the canonical city-facing entrance to the megadungeon beneath Mount Waterdeep. Owner: Durnan, who has run the Portal since before most living Waterdhavians were born. Long-lived by adventurer's standards (rumored dwarf-blood or Undermountain-acquired longevity magic). Laconic, fair, intolerant of disturbances. Quarterstaff behind the bar is famously more than it appears. Knows Laeral personally; has known every Open Lord. Mirt the Moneylender is a frequent patron at the central common-room table, former Harper, extensive city connections. The Well is stone-ringed, 40 feet diameter, ringed by waist-high wall, heavy iron grating lowered at night, winch-and-rope assembly for paid descent (1 gp standard fee). Adventurers, merchants, scholars from Font of Knowledge, Harpers, and occasional nobility form the regular clientele. Shi'van has not been a direct patron — her Waterdeep social geography runs Sea Ward / North Ward rather than the Castle Ward adventurer belt — but the Portal is strategically relevant as rumor nexus, Undermountain/Skullport interface, potential Mirt encounter site, and default adventurer-recruitment venue. Firth's Observer Network includes passive monitoring of common-room conversation.
WotC canon: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist (5E), Dungeon of the Mad Mage (5E), City of Splendors: Waterdeep (3.5E), Volo's Guide to Waterdeep (2E).
Inn staff; no Baen or Observer Network presence. Discreet but standard-commercial security.

Merchant District inn, Neverwinter. Shi'van's registered lodging during the Session 34 stay (Days 701-717). Check-in 25th Eleint 1493 DR, seventh bell. First B. Taranis operations contact within one hour of check-in — dinner invitation delivered. Seren independently identified a separate watcher at the gate registry during the same window — Aldric economic analyst, not B. Taranis. The Crosscurrent was Shi'van's sleep base for the stay; day-hours transferred to Aldwich Lane workshop.

Sandrew the Wise (High Loremaster of Oghma, Chief cleric, administrative head of the Font, long-serving, institutionally careful, trusted scholarly referee across the Sword Coast). ~30 ordained Loremasters residing on premises, subdivided by specialty (theological lore, historical record, natural philosophy, magical theory, commercial and genealogical archives). ~20 Acolytes (junior clergy in training, staff front desk, guide casual researchers, maintain catalogue). ~40 Lay Scholars at any time (rotating cohort with temple-granted research access — visiting Candlekeep academics, noble-sponsored genealogists, Watchful Order research affiliates, scholars from other institutions). Permanent magical climate control (temperature, humidity, pest suppression) maintained by clergy. Ward-sealed Closed Collection subsection (restricted to senior clergy and writ-bearing researchers). No standing martial garrison — Oghmite institutional neutrality and magical archive protections are the security.

Temple of Oghma and largest public library in Waterdeep. Castle Ward, Street of Bells. Three-story domed stone building, 80-ft rotunda under copper-sheathed dome, classical architecture (columns, pediment carved with Oghma's scroll-and-branch symbol). Second-most-significant bibliographic institution in Faerûn after Candlekeep — considerably more accessible (Candlekeep requires book-donation tribute; Font admits legitimate researchers). Holdings span theology, history, geography, natural philosophy, non-practical magical theory, genealogy, commercial records, administrative archives predating many Waterdhavian institutions' own records. Cataloguing system is Oghmite (four centuries of curatorial refinement). Permanent climate control — temperature stable, humidity managed, pest-sealed. Closed Collection subsection ward-sealed, restricted access, holds dangerous/fragile/politically sensitive material. High Loremaster: Sandrew the Wise (elderly human, long-serving, institutionally neutral, trusted scholarly referee). ~30 ordained Loremasters, ~20 Acolytes, ~40 rotating Lay Scholars. Campaign relevance: Drathen Baen'und craft-lineage research pathway (four centuries of commercial/genealogical Waterdhavian records); Gallows-Marked prophecy complementary to Sage Kellam's Candlekeep material; Institut non-practical magical theory research; Karak Durath archival context (Dessarin corridor, displaced dwarven clans, Besilmer-era fortresses); Rosenna Thatch's research base as lay scholar. Institution's principal strategic asset is neutrality — hardliner coalition, Masked Lords, Ship Kurth, Aldenmere all find same courteous welcome as Shi'van.
WotC canon: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist (5E), City of Splendors: Waterdeep (3.5E), Volo's Guide to Waterdeep (2E), Faiths and Pantheons (3E Oghma domain).

Guildmaster Torben Wicksworth (principal authority, ground-floor rear office, co-chair of the 216-143 Wicksworth partnership alliance vote). Senior Lamplighters' Council (5-member adjudicative body including Wicksworth, meets in second-floor chamber). Dispatch clerk at ground-floor desk (daily route assignments, knows every active lamplighter by sight). Registry clerk on second floor (pension-records archive, apprenticeship-completion documentation). 804 active members distributed across all city wards (down from 912 a decade ago, 40% recruitment reduction documented). Notable members: Aldous Brent (63, 41 years, Castle Ward route, retiring in 2 years, Session 8C hearing witness); Gareth Dunwell (Ward 3 lamplighter, Session 21 Commerce Court hearing witness). No standing martial garrison — guild security is lamplighter discipline plus commercial-grade locks on the second-floor pension-records archive. Pension records duplicated at Castle Waterdeep judicial annex as institutional insurance.

Home of the Lamplighters' Guild of Waterdeep. Trades Ward, a block north of the working-class commercial corridor. Two-story brick building. Ground floor: dispatch office (large slate board mapping city's lamp-post network by ward, chalk maintenance marks), equipment storage, cart yard access, common room with coal stove for pre-dawn/post-dusk gatherings, Guildmaster Wicksworth's office (at back, small, desk facing the yard, his apprentice-completion certificate framed behind him). Second floor: registry clerk's office, pension-records archive (40 years of certified employment records — duplicated at Castle Waterdeep annex as institutional insurance), apprenticeship-completion documentation (114 entries over past decade), meeting chamber with oak benches and raised platform for Wicksworth's speaking position. Wicksworth filed the Session 8C Section 22 petition against the Promethean Device (Day 505); lost 3-2 at the Day 510 hearing; read Shi'van's Promethean Lamp Post transition proposal post-hearing and did not look away. Post-Commerce Court Day 592: Gareth Dunwell's testimony established the guild's working-class legitimacy as part of Shi'van's 4-1 vindication. Oakheart's Commerce Court speech publicly staked the guild's position to Shi'van's follow-through on maintenance and pensions. The Promethean Lamp Post Infrastructure Program (2,000 posts, 300-340 sustained positions) depends on the guild's cooperation for maintenance contract; the guild's pension future depends on the program's economic stability. Northern Shield Assurance's Pension Bridge Endowment (25,000gp) backs the transition period; Wicksworth is Toril Shield Assurance's Guild Advisory Chair. Relationship is neither alliance nor enmity — grudging ongoing institutional engagement forced into partnership by infrastructure mathematics. 'Best antagonist the campaign has produced — right about everything except the conclusion.' Rosenna Thatch (Waterdeep Sentinel freelance) interviewed Wicksworth in the meeting chamber before the Session 8C hearing, two-hour session.
Session 8C hearing week log (Days 505-510, Ches 1493); Session 21 Commerce Court log (Day 592); Session 29 Pension Bridge Endowment structure; Oakheart Dock Ward testimony transcript.

No formal authority. Rotating informal hierarchies, shifting season by season — whoever currently has the most muscle, the most reliable knife, or the most convincing protection claim. Current strongest figure typically unknown to Watch records by the time those records are filed. ~12 boat-rowers (semi-permanent figures working skiffs through the Gut, closest thing to infrastructure, paid ears for outsiders). A handful of wise-women (older, long-surviving medicine-women, midwives, who wash the dead for burial at sea — do not take sides, do not name names, accept payment in food or fabric). Xanathar Guild contractors (unnamed, recognizable, Mistshore as deniable labor pool for Guild operations; recruited, used, often disposed). Watch does not patrol Mistshore — enters only on specific body-retrieval writs. No institutional governance. No guild society. The law is whatever is currently locally enforceable.

Floating shantytown on southern Dock Ward waterfront. ~1000-1500 destitute residents on any given day — shipwreck survivors, refugees outside guild society, broken dock-workers, addicts, deserters, fugitives, their children. Built on abandoned ships lashed together, stilt-houses in harbor mud, plank-walks rising and falling with tide. Three quarters: Shore Quarter (lean-tos and shacks on dry ground), Stilt Quarter (pole-platforms above high tide), Floating Quarter (hulk-cluster and houseboats). The Gut (narrow channels navigable by skiff, boat-rowers hire for 1-2 cp). Outer Wreck Field (partially submerged abandoned hulks, unsafe boundary with open harbor). No Watch presence except body-retrieval writs. No Guild-Under-the-Well interest. Xanathar Guild uses as deniable labor pool. Boat-rowers are accessible intelligence interface (paid per inquiry). Wise-women provide midwifery, medicine, burial services. For Shi'van's operations: hard geographic boundary. No drow presence survives the threshold. Firth's Observer Network maps Mistshore's margins; Peri's underworld apparatus handles extractions inside; refugee intake does not reach Mistshore-proper because the institutional identity has been lost. Campaign relevance: missing-persons trail termination, Xanathar Guild recruiter tracking, refugee program structural limitation, rare high-stakes scene venue.
WotC canon: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist (5E), City of Splendors: Waterdeep (3.5E), Mistshore FR references across multiple editions.
Husteem household staff. Lady Melinda Husteem direct. Tessavere salon staff at relay point. No dedicated Baen'und personnel on-site.

Noble-class distribution channel for Baen'und commercial products (Promethean Device luxury variants, Summer Crown, Institut garments, Lanternlight Purse, future commercial products). 60/40 Shi'van/Husteem partnership split on noble sales only. Operational base: Husteem family residence, Castle Ward. Origin: 'The Fountain Handshake' in Coins Ward, Session 8A. Partnership gross approximately 1,900 gp/month (Shi'van 1,140, Husteem 760). Brand pre-positioned through Lady Tessavere's salon via Melinda Husteem intermediaries before Blackwatch Lane showroom opening. Marcel complication (early sessions, family social exile) resolved through Tessavere placement and Marcel's standing as Institut Creative Director. Channel stable at Day 717.
Promethean Device Creation Registry (334e8214-84b0-81c8); Promethean Device — Husteem Channel Monthly (342e8214-84b0-81cb); 14 Blackwatch Lane Showroom (347e8214-84b0-8130)

No standing presence. Kenafin embedded asset (provisionally Thessaly Wren) dormant since Day 620. Bregan D'aerthe active two-way collection (Kimmuriel Oblodra reading product). Unidentified fourth party maintaining "third box" as response address (Gallows-Marked-aware, anonymous approach Day 725). Multi-box architecture inferred from Session 36 letter.

Kenafin dead drop + BD two-way channel + anonymous fourth-party correspondence site. Candle Street, Waterdeep. Third lamp post north of the Plinth landmark, east side, hollow post cap for Kenafin. Multiple boxes inferred (Session 36 references 'third box'). Shi'van deposited Day 684; BD collected by Day 688. Embedded asset's final known deposit Day 620. Anonymous letter invoking Gallows-Marked arrived Day 725 requesting response via third box (yes/no/a-for-delay). Most intelligence-active single site in Shi'van's operational picture — do not surveil directly.

~30 Groundskeepers (permanent staff, joint City/noble-endowment employment, grass/trees/paths/tomb facade maintenance, Veilstone and Ashbrook families hold hereditary positions). ~8 Sealkeepers (rotating clerical detail from Spires of the Morning, Halls of Justice, House of the Moon — quarterly seal inspection and ritual maintenance). 12 Nightkeeper Watch constables (specialized City Watch detachment, post-sunset patrol, undead containment training, silvered weapons and torches, signal horn for clerical response). 4 Gatekeepers (civilian Coffinmarch Gate and North Gate staff, public hours only, log arrivals, direct mourners, not armed). Clerical responders on-call from contributing temples. No human living population after dusk — the gates close, the Watch patrols, and nothing else should be here.

Waterdeep's principal cemetery. Walled and gated necropolis in the city's north between North Ward and the Trollwalls. ~2 miles of stone wall perimeter (12-15 ft tall, wrought-iron spikes), four gated entrances (Coffinmarch Gate south principal, North Gate residential-adjacent, 2 service gates). Interior grounds ~quarter-mile by third-mile. Landscaped as formal park: stone avenues, gravel secondary paths, grass, mature oak/ash/yew/cypress (oldest predate city founding). Waterdhavian burial tradition emphasizes above-ground stone interment — family mausoleums, guild memorial halls, individual tombs. Key sections: Lords' Walk (principal central avenue, former Open Lords and posthumously-identified Masked Lords), Heroes' Garden (adventurers who died in Undermountain service, Durnan's patronage), paupers' section (simpler markers for those unable to afford above-ground interment). Every tomb ward-sealed with inscription; quarterly inspection and renewal. Public by day (family mourning, noble picnics, children playing); sealed by dusk; nothing living inside walls after dark, nothing dead should leave. Nightkeeper Watch specialized detachment containment-patrols post-sunset. Clerical responders on-call from Spires of the Morning, Halls of Justice, House of the Moon. Campaign relevance: Shi'van's Gallows-Marked Shepherd status intersects thematically but not operationally yet; potential memento mori commercial opportunity for Institut; undead incident venue if campaign requires; Heroes' Garden Durnan patronage channel for Undermountain-adjacent casualties; Kenafin theological-assessor possible interest in Waterdhavian burial practice.
WotC canon: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist (5E), City of Splendors: Waterdeep (3.5E), Volo's Guide to Waterdeep (2E), The City of Splendors FR module.
Hunding Canal — Baen Continental Waterway System

1,400 permanent staff total at full operation. Bloodaxe Legion security coverage system-wide (~600 personnel), augmented by crystal network monitoring. Each operational lock station: minimum 6 Bloodaxe guards + Hunding technicians + lock keepers (~20 permanent per station). Formicorps tunnel colonies under Baen control for maintenance and emergency repair.

Colloquial name for the full Baen Continental Waterway System. 600-mile infrastructure project 1494-1500 DR. Continental span Sword Coast North to Anauroch. Three-phase structure: Western Network (operational), Hunding Mountain Lock System (~30% complete at Early 1495 DR, 12 lock stations across 80 miles and 2,400 ft elevation change), Eastern Extension via Desertsmouth Tunnel + Anauroch glacier terminus (planning). Partnership with Hunding family clockwork engineers (name-source). Estimated total cost 12-15M gp. Net annual profit at full operation ~750K gp. Payback 8-9 years excluding strategic value. Canal completion is the active Dalelands casus belli driver at current campaign position — every Grey Banner convoy blockade, every Sembian commissary rejection, every Zhentarim broadsheet mockery is documented toward the 1497-1498 DR continental war. Sembian Terminus Proposal exists as canonical strategic option (Sembia builds Section C, gets 5% gross revenue in perpetuity).

Unidentified Ship Kurth / Bregan D'aerthe receiving personnel. Specific proprietor and internal operation unmapped. NRTC commercial inquiry active via Marcus Ironhand's driver (Session 31-32, cover establishing, ~tenday from Day 663 to operational readiness). Ship Kurth evaluators at Sleeping Serpent Waterdeep (Session 32) constrain active exploitation tempo.

Luskan-end terminus of Petra Voss communication channel. Fish Street, Luskan. Weekly courier pouch (textile samples + invoices + hidden surveillance reports) delivered here from Northgate stables Waterdeep via Thornhold/Red Larch/Triboar route. Identified Session 31 but UNMAPPED. NRTC commercial inquiry active mapping vector (Marcus's driver, commercial cover, Session 32 cover establishing). Ship Kurth = Beniago Kurth = Bregan D'aerthe (Session 33 reframe) — so endpoint may be a BD intelligence endpoint, which reframes the channel's strategic meaning. Voss family (Petra + brother Renald) link this to Northwatch Consulting / Ravencrest territorial operation. DO NOT RAID — mapping only, preserve knowledge advantage.

No living personnel. Four animate stone constructs carved into Mount Waterdeep's flanks. Each ~90 ft tall humanoid granite form. Dormant under normal conditions; activation by Open Lord authority (primary) or emergency Masked Lords quorum (never used in living memory). Archmage (Vajra Safahr) holds standing oversight writ: weekly Griffon Cavalry aerial inspection, quarterly Watchful Order magical condition assessment, immediate anomaly notification to Castle Waterdeep. Masked Lords provide consultative authority; Open Lord decides. Never walked in living memory; historical activations documented at Font of Knowledge archive level. Weapons capability: individual statue combat capacity historically demonstrated but not quantified; engagement with 90-ft humanoid stone construct produces city-scale effects regardless of specific combat stats. Standing defensive orders: invasion, existential magical assault, catastrophic harbor breach. Thresholds for activation are not public knowledge (adversary opacity as deterrent).

Four massive animate stone constructs carved into Mount Waterdeep's flanks at strategic elevations — Waterdeep's emergency defensive reserve and iconic Sword Coast standing wonders. Each ~90 ft tall, humanoid body-plan, carved directly from living granite of the mountain face (feet merge with rock beneath, separate on activation). Four positions: Eastern Sentinel (highest prominence, most commonly visible from inhabited Waterdeep), Southern Harbor-Watcher (upper southern flank, visible from harbor/Seatower/Castle Ward), Western Sea-Watcher (upper western face above sea cliff, visible to approaching vessels, widest observation field in city), Northern Trollwall Guardian (upper northern ridge, land-approach defensive posture). Activation requires Open Lord authority (Laeral Silverhand) as primary trigger + Archmage (Vajra Safahr) magical preparation + Masked Lords consultative input. Historical activations documented at Font of Knowledge (multiple pre-Time-of-Troubles defenses). Not walked in living memory. Activation is political nuclear option — city-wide evacuation triggers, harbor defenses maximum readiness, Griffon Cavalry aerial overwatch, Seatower alert bell, Masked Lords emergency session, Lords' Alliance notification, commercial suspension, months-to-years recovery. Campaign relevance: environmental backdrop (skyline), existential threat ceiling (campaign stakes cap), institutional intersection via Laeral/Vajra/Watchful Order/Institut partnership. Not current operational geography. WotC canonical designations vary across editions; campaign-consistent designations used here with Font of Knowledge as research pathway for specific canonical names if needed.
WotC canon: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist (5E), Dungeon of the Mad Mage (5E), City of Splendors: Waterdeep (3.5E), Volo's Guide to Waterdeep (2E), Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3E.
